diagrams.title: Buy Verified Earnings; Then Protect Them
diagrams.subtitle: Five linked workstreams from acquisition thesis to the first 100 days.
diagrams.assumptions_note: First-deal timing is 4–10 months. The 100-day operating plan starts after closing, not after initial outreach. Recognized revenue is acquired-business sales, not purchase price, borrowed principal, seller proceeds, or transaction volume.
diagrams.caption: Advance only with the evidence named in each stage; keep the customer-retention plan connected to the purchase agreement.

stages.label: Define the buy box
stages.detail: Specify geography, transferable licenses, customer concentration limits, operator replacement cost, and a $30,000–$120,000 buyer-capital envelope.

stages.label: Verify earnings
stages.detail: Tie QuickBooks exports to bank deposits, tax returns, receivables aging, payroll, and customer contracts; remove unsupported add-backs and identify maintenance capex.

stages.label: Structure the purchase
stages.detail: Model lender debt and seller notes separately; define working-capital delivery, asset allocation, lien releases, representations, indemnities, and required contract transfers.

stages.label: Transfer operating control
stages.detail: Reconcile closing funds, verify insurance and license continuity, transfer authorized bank access, and test payroll and customer billing before retiring seller access.

stages.label: Run the 100-day plan
stages.detail: Track weekly collections, customer retention, backlog, service defects, and covenant headroom; automate reporting only after ledger ownership and exception handling work.

diagrams.title: One Cohort, Five Evidence Filters
diagrams.subtitle: An illustrative 120-target search cohort narrows to two signed LOIs.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Counts describe one hypothetical cohort observed through a common cutoff, not monthly throughput or an industry benchmark. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. A signed LOI does not establish a completed acquisition.
diagrams.caption: Stage conversions are 40%, 50%, 33.33%, and 25%; cumulative target-to-LOI conversion is 2 / 120 = 1.67%.

stages.label: Qualified targets
stages.detail: Deduplicate broker and direct-owner leads in Airtable; record business identity, geography, sector, and a specific reason the ownership model fits.

stages.label: Owner conversations
stages.detail: Confirm seller authority, transition intentions, expected timing, and willingness to provide operating records before requesting confidential customer-level material.

stages.label: Usable data rooms
stages.detail: Execute confidentiality terms and obtain sufficient ledger, payroll, tax, and receivables records to compare the seller narrative with recorded operating activity.

stages.label: Diligence-ready candidates
stages.detail: Complete preliminary earnings normalization, concentration review, and debt-service stress testing; reserve full third-party QoE expenditure for the selected transaction.

stages.label: Signed LOIs
stages.detail: Negotiate price mechanics, exclusivity, diligence access, and closing conditions sequentially where capacity demands; neither LOI is counted as revenue or a closed deal.

diagrams.title: From $1,875,000 Sales to $243,750 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the Base-Case 13.0% annual net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Canonical annual outcomes: Conservative $750,000 sales at 8% equals $60,000 owner net; Base $1,875,000 at 13.0% equals $243,750; Scaled $3,000,000 at 18% equals $540,000. Expense allocations below are illustrative, not additional scorecard inputs. Net is after interest and before principal repayments; no separate owner-level income-tax calculation is supplied.
diagrams.caption: Render sales as the opening total, four negative expense movements, and owner net as the closing total: $1,875,000 − $900,000 − $450,000 − $187,500 − $93,750 = $243,750. Do not add the closing total as another movement.

stages.label: Acquired-business sales
stages.detail: Use earned sales from the operating company; exclude acquisition debt proceeds, equity contributions, sales tax collected for remittance, and purchase consideration.

stages.label: Direct fulfillment costs
stages.detail: Allocate materials, outside fulfillment, and other direct costs here; exclude pod payroll already assigned below. The remaining gross profit is $975,000.

stages.label: Recurring pod labor
stages.detail: Illustrative loaded labor and recurring contractor expense averages $37,500 monthly across the core pod; validate local wages, benefits, and contractor scope.

stages.label: Other operating expense
stages.detail: Budget $15,625 monthly for occupancy, insurance, software, and remaining operating charges. Together with pod labor, recurring overhead is $53,125 monthly, excluding direct costs.

stages.label: Interest expense
stages.detail: Interest averages $7,812.50 monthly in this allocation. Debt principal is not an earnings expense; model its cash requirement separately using actual amortization schedules.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Divide $243,750 by $1,875,000 to recover 13.0%. Then separately bridge earnings to available cash for principal, working-capital changes, capex, and distributions.

diagrams.title: Collection Yield by Acquisition Sub-Niche
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative dollars banked within 30 days per $100 invoiced.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Five independent underwriting examples use hypothetical collection assumptions, not observed sector averages. Numeric values are percentages of an invoice cohort collected within 30 days. Collections are measured before payment-processing fees; slower collection does not automatically mean bad debt.
diagrams.caption: Compare cash conversion rather than mistaking payment-rail receipts for incremental sales or owner profit. Replace every assumption with target-specific invoice and bank evidence.

stages.label: Managed IT services
stages.detail: Illustrative recurring ACH cohort: verify debit authorizations, return histories, disputed service credits, and whether customer contracts survive the ownership change.

stages.label: Commercial cleaning
stages.detail: Illustrative ACH and check cohort: inspect customer payment runs, site acceptance requirements, invoice disputes, and payroll funded before customer collection.

stages.label: Equipment maintenance
stages.detail: Illustrative card and ACH cohort: reconcile signed service tickets, parts charges, processor deductions, refund exposure, and commercial-account credit terms.

stages.label: Specialty distribution
stages.detail: Illustrative trade-credit cohort: test delivery evidence, returns, deductions, inventory funding, and customer credit limits rather than relying on invoice totals.

stages.label: Commercial field services
stages.detail: Illustrative milestone-billing cohort: identify retainage, purchase-order mismatches, disputed completion certificates, and collection delays hidden inside reported receivables.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Committing Closing Funds
diagrams.subtitle: Each affirmative branch advances; unresolved evidence returns to diligence.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Apply jurisdiction-specific employment, tax, licensing, and secured-transactions rules to the actual deal structure. SBA requirements apply when using the relevant program; lender covenants and disclosure obligations depend on executed terms.
diagrams.caption: Treat the four nodes as sequential decisions. An unresolved branch requires a documented cure, revised economics, or withdrawal before funds are committed.

stages.label: Can title transfer cleanly?
stages.detail: Search applicable UCC filing offices and inspect liens outside that system. UCC § 9-315 generally preserves security interests after disposition unless an exception applies; obtain secured-party releases and payoff evidence.

stages.label: Are tax terms executable?
stages.value: Yes: advance; unresolved: revise closing terms
stages.detail: For applicable asset acquisitions, align allocation and Form 8594 reporting under 26 U.S.C. § 1060. Review state successor-tax exposure, payroll remittances, clearance requirements, and tax-related indemnity support.

stages.label: Can people and licenses continue?
stages.value: Yes: advance; unresolved: cure continuity risks
stages.detail: Test overtime exposure under 29 U.S.C. § 207, applicable WARN duties under §§ 2101–2102, state employment rules, and license transfer restrictions. Obtain required consents and verify customer assignment terms.

stages.label: Does the debt structure survive stress?
stages.value: Yes: proceed; unresolved: resize or withdraw
stages.detail: For SBA transactions, review 13 CFR §§ 120.110, 120.150, and 120.160 plus current program requirements. Disclose seller notes and side agreements; stress principal, interest, customer loss, and covenant headroom.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats; Two Explicit Scale Additions
diagrams.subtitle: Conservative and Base: 2 FT + 2 C (4 people). Scaled: 3 FT + 3 C (6 people).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each of the first four entries has numeric value 1 and represents one active core person: two full-time operators and two contractors. The final two entries have numeric value 0 because they are inactive in the core configuration; activating one FT and one C produces the six-person Scaled pod. Contractors are people, not full-time-equivalent claims. External vendor and trade sub-crews are charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not counted as internal pod seats.
diagrams.caption: The acquisition lead owns capital allocation; the general manager combines operating, service, and retention leadership. Two specialist contractors cover legal and financial workstreams. Add an operations lead and a systems contractor only at scale: four active core seats plus two optional seats, not six core hires.

stages.label: Acquisition lead
stages.detail: Own purchase discipline, lender relationships, investment decisions, seller negotiations, and the weekly review of liquidity and customer concentration.

stages.label: General manager
stages.detail: Own the operating result, scheduling, vendor coordination, service standards, customer retention, and execution of the post-close 100-day integration plan. Retain delivery accountability when external vendors perform customer work.

stages.label: Transaction counsel
stages.detail: Review transaction disclosures, purchase terms, lien releases, license transfers, employment issues, and post-close claims within a defined engagement.

stages.label: Fractional controller, QoE and tax specialist
stages.detail: One appropriately qualified contractor combines earnings verification, working-capital review, and tax-allocation support with post-close reconciliations, cash forecasting, receivables oversight, and covenant reporting. Define scope and capacity explicitly rather than implying extra seats.

stages.label: Operations lead
stages.value: Scale-only addition: FT 3 of 3; inactive in core
stages.detail: Activate one additional full-time person only in the six-person Scaled configuration to own scheduling, vendor capacity, backlog, and service-quality controls, freeing the general manager for broader operating oversight.

stages.label: Systems and workflow specialist
stages.value: Scale-only addition: contractor 3 of 3; inactive in core
stages.detail: Activate one additional contractor only in the Scaled configuration to configure accounting integrations, access controls, backups, and reporting automation; document recovery procedures and exception ownership.

diagrams.title: Allocate a $75,000 Reference Startup Budget
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets compare $30,000 lean, $75,000 reference, and $120,000 expanded plans.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The canonical startup-capital range is $30,000–$120,000 USD. The $75,000 central/reference plan allocates 40%, 10%, 30%, and 20% across four buckets. Lean and expanded plans use the same illustrative weights, not claims that every transaction is feasible at either boundary. Size acquisition financing and required liquidity against transaction-specific evidence.
diagrams.caption: Numeric values are reference-plan USD and sum to $75,000: $30,000 + $7,500 + $22,500 + $15,000. Lean allocations sum to $30,000: $12,000 + $3,000 + $9,000 + $6,000. Expanded allocations sum to $120,000: $48,000 + $12,000 + $36,000 + $24,000. Buyer capital is neither recognized sales nor total enterprise value.

stages.label: Purchase equity contribution
stages.detail: Allocate $12,000 of the $30,000 lean plan, $30,000 of the $75,000 reference plan, and $48,000 of the $120,000 expanded plan. Size debt separately; confirm lender equity requirements and seller-note treatment before treating any note as qualifying injection.

stages.label: Diligence and closing costs
stages.detail: Allocate $3,000 of the $30,000 lean plan, $7,500 of the $75,000 reference plan, and $12,000 of the $120,000 expanded plan for QoE, counsel, tax work, searches, and transaction expenses. Validate quoted fees before proceeding; separate one-time engagement charges from recurring contractor expense.

stages.label: Opening working-capital reserve
stages.detail: Allocate $9,000 of the $30,000 lean plan, $22,500 of the $75,000 reference plan, and $36,000 of the $120,000 expanded plan. Fund collection gaps and seasonality after reconciling seller-delivered working capital to the negotiated closing adjustment.

stages.label: Integration and contingency liquidity
stages.detail: Allocate $6,000 of the $30,000 lean plan, $15,000 of the $75,000 reference plan, and $24,000 of the $120,000 expanded plan for migration, retention, and repair contingencies. Cash released for one purpose cannot simultaneously remain available for another.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Decision-Ready Acquisition Search
diagrams.subtitle: Build an evidence pipeline without pretending the first deal closes in a month.
diagrams.assumptions_note: This is a pre-acquisition launch sprint. First-deal timing remains 4–10 months; the 100-day turnaround starts after closing. Numeric values are milestone endpoint days.
diagrams.caption: Complete one inspectable operating artifact each week. A missing seller document becomes a tracked diligence issue, not an invented input to the debt model.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Deliver the buy box and capital plan
stages.detail: Assign the acquisition lead; document sector exclusions, buyer liquidity, operator capacity, and concentration limits. Build the four-bucket capital worksheet and identify lender and specialist interview targets.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.detail: Configure Airtable stages and deduplication; begin broker and owner outreach. Record response evidence, confidentiality terms, seller authority, and requested records without treating the illustrative funnel as a quota.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Deliver the first evidence-backed screening memo
stages.detail: For a responsive target, reconcile available statements to deposits, review customer concentration, and build an interest-and-principal schedule. If records are insufficient, issue a precise evidence request instead.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Deliver the pursue, revise, or reject decision
stages.detail: Review the four pre-flight checks, document downside liquidity, and price unresolved liabilities. Prepare LOI terms only for a supported candidate; otherwise revise the search and preserve diligence capital.
